questions.question: How do scientists classify living organisms into groups within larger groups?
options: By looking at the similarities and differences in their physical and genetic features.
By sorting them solely by their geographic location and habitat.
By grouping them based only on their size and weight.
By arranging them randomly to make them easier to study.

questions.question: What is the correct hierarchy of classification groups from the largest to the smallest?
options: Species down to kingdom
Kingdom down to species
Genus down to kingdom
Family down to phylum

questions.question: Which of the following is true about larger classification groups, such as kingdoms, compared to smaller groups?
options: They contain fewer organisms with many similarities in their features.
They contain more organisms with fewer similarities in their features.
They contain fewer organisms with no features in common.
They contain more organisms that are genetically identical to each other.

questions.question: What defines a group of organisms as belonging to the same species?
options: They live in the same area and eat the exact same food.
They have similar features and genes, and can reproduce to make fertile offspring.
They look identical and have exactly the same life expectancy.
They can reproduce together, even if their offspring are always infertile.

questions.question: In the binomial system of naming organisms, what two classification groups do the names represent?
options: Kingdom and Phylum
Class and Order
Genus and Species
Family and Genus

questions.question: Besides visible external features, how else can scientists classify organisms into groups?
options: By measuring their heart rate in different weather conditions.
By studying their characteristics at the microscopic, cellular level.
By observing their behavior only during the night.
By comparing their speed of movement over long distances.

questions.question: Which of the following cellular features is found in plant, fungi, and bacterial cells, but is always absent in animal cells?
options: A cell wall
A nucleus
Cytoplasm
A cell membrane

questions.question: If a scientist discovers a new single-celled organism that has no nucleus, which kingdom does it most likely belong to?
options: Animals
Plants
Fungi
Bacteria

questions.question: What is the main purpose of using a classification key in biology?
options: To count the total number of organisms in a specific ecosystem.
To find out which groups different organisms are classified into.
To measure the rate of photosynthesis in green plants.
To predict how a species will evolve over millions of years.

questions.question: What describes a classification key?
options: A list of definitions of scientific terms in alphabetical order.
A series of questions about the features of organisms.
A set of diagrams showing the internal organs of animals.
A table showing the chemical composition of different cell walls.

questions.question: Why is classification an important tool for scientists studying biodiversity?
options: It helps us organise and make sense of the vast variety of living things.
It allows us to change the DNA of organisms to make them more useful.
It guarantees that no more species will go extinct in the future.
It simplifies the process of naming new chemical elements.

questions.question: When carrying out fieldwork to study organisms, what is a key scientific process that should be performed?
options: Relying entirely on memory to recall the organisms seen.
Making, recording, and interpreting observations of organisms.
Collecting all organisms and keeping them in a laboratory permanently.
Modifying the physical features of the organisms to see how they adapt.

questions.question: How can a student identify an unknown wild plant while working in the field?
options: By guessing its name based on its flower colour alone.
By using a classification key to identify and classify it.
By comparing its size to a standard domestic houseplant.
By waiting for it to grow fruit before making any decision.

questions.question: When studying organisms in their natural habitat, which practice represents working safely and responsibly?
options: Removing entire plants and nests to study them back at home.
Minimising harm to living organisms and avoiding disruption to ecosystems.
Introducing new species to see how the native species react.
Clearing away all surrounding vegetation to get a better view.

questions.question: A horse and a donkey can mate to produce a mule, but mules are sterile. What does this tell us about horses and donkeys?
options: They belong to the same species because they can mate.
They belong to different species because their offspring is not fertile.
They belong to different kingdoms because they have different features.
They are the same species because they share many similar genes.
